endorsements.quote: ACP firmly believes that AI-enabled technologies should complement and not supplant the logic and decision making of physicians and other clinicians.
ACP recommends that patients, physicians, and other clinicians be made aware, when possible, that AI tools are likely being used in medical treatment and decision making.
ACP calls for AI model development data to include data from diverse populations for which resulting models may be used.
This necessarily includes end-user testing in diverse real-world clinical contexts, using real patient demographics, and peer-reviewed research.

To promote patient safety and transparency, ACP calls for transparency, clarity, and education for physicians and other clinicians about where AI-generated information is entering workflows and ensuring that physician knowledge and discretion can supersede AI-generated “defaults,” when appropriate.
Training and testing data sources and attributes should be transparent and accessible to physicians, regulators, and auditors.

unlisted_practices: Provide training on AI at all levels of medical education so physicians understand AI-enabled health care systems.
Have the FDA and ONC engage stakeholders to develop standardized, easy-to-understand model labels and reporting checklists covering model quality, performance, and use criteria.
Establish readily available mechanisms for clinicians to flag errors in AI output and for developers to correct them.
Report suspected AI-related adverse events to regulators such as the FDA and log them in public databases.
Establish a coordinated federal AI strategy built on a unified governance framework.
Avoid anthropomorphic language such as think, learn, and hallucinate when describing AI models.
Design AI tools to reduce clinician burden and test them with real end users before deployment.
Use continuous improvement processes with feedback mechanisms for AI in health care.
Conduct algorithmic impact assessments, audits, and postmarket monitoring of AI tools.
Fund research on the clinical and ethical implications and disparate effects of AI.
